title: emergencyWithdraw does not settle accrual, redirecting the exiting user's pro-rata emissions to remaining stakers
description: emergencyWithdraw sets user.amount = 0 and decrements totalStaked, but deliberately does not call _updatePool()/ _syncBudget() per the spec. The consequence is that all accrual over the interval [lastRewardTime, block.timestamp] is attributed to the new, smaller totalStaked on the next _updatePool. The exiting user's fair share of that interval is not left in the rewardBudget (correctly, since _updatePool wasn't called), but is instead silently redistributed to whoever is still staked — because the accRewardPerShare increment uses the reduced denominator in the subsequent call.
economicImpact: The emergency-withdrawer forfeits pending rewards (intended), but those rewards are NOT returned to the budget or burned — they are shifted into a higher per-share accumulator for the remaining stakers on the next accrual. Remaining stakers receive more than their arithmetic pro-rata for the window in which the exit happened. This can be exploited by a staker who controls multiple accounts: one account stakes a large amount, emergency-withdraws just before a major pull(), leaving the other account(s) to absorb the full elapsed-time emission at the new denominator.
attackPath:
1. Attacker stakes 1000 units on account A and 1 unit on account B. totalStaked = 1001.
2. 1 day passes; pending reward for the day = R, distributed 1000/1001 to A and 1/1001 to B.
3. Attacker calls emergencyWithdraw on A. totalStaked = 1. user A's accrued share of R is forfeited as pending — but crucially _updatePool is NOT called at this point.
4. Next user action triggers _updatePool for the elapsed interval [lastRewardTime, now]. accRewardPerShare += (reward * 1e18) / 1. Account B's pending explodes: B captures effectively the full day's emission despite owning only 1/1001 of the stake during that day.
5. Attacker claims on B.

Note: this is partially-mitigated by the fact that in normal flows _updatePool is called on every user action, so [lastRewardTime, now] is usually short. But because emergencyWithdraw is callable while paused, an attacker can coordinate exits at strategic moments.
quantifiedLoss: Gain to remaining stakers = (exiting_user.amount / old_totalStaked) * reward_over_[lastRewardTime, now]. If an attacker controls both exit and a small remainder, they can effectively claim rewards that would otherwise have gone to themselves under the full stake. Bounded by the reward accrued in the interval since the last _updatePool call.
recommendation: Call _updatePool() (NOT _syncBudget — the spec correctly wants to skip dispatcher interactions here) at the start of emergencyWithdraw to settle accrual under the existing denominator. The spec's rationale for skipping accrual is to avoid reverts from a broken dispatcher hook, which _updatePool alone does not touch. Settling accrual before the denominator changes removes the redistribution bonus without introducing the dispatcher risk the spec was guarding against.
